newsitem.title: INDIA: Hopes of end to political crisis lift Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Hopes of end to political crisis lift Delhi shares.

text.p: Delhi share prices opened higher on Tuesday, buoyed by expectations the United Front coalition would form a government with Congress support, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 4.72 points higher at 757.77 after 30 minutes of trade.
B.K. Nagpal of brokers B.B. Portfolios said the prospect that a new coalition government would be formed, averting mid-term polls, spurred buying.
It was the first trading session since Saturday, as the market was closed on Monday for a holiday.
The Congress party on Monday offered to support the United Front coalition provided the alliance replaced its leader, caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Deve Gowda, who was defeated in a parliamentary confidence vote on Friday, told his 15-party coalition on Sunday that he would step down if his partners so decided.
Traders said expectations that the 1997/98 budget would be passed by parliament also pushed up prices.
"The market is concerned about two things, avoidance of mid-term polls and passage of the budget," said one broker.
Parliament has agreed to take up the federal budget next week, but it was unclear if the political crisis and amendments would blunt its thrust.
Reliance Industries rose 5.00 rupees to 270.00 on buying by speculators and foreign institutional investors (FIIs), brokers said.
State Bank of India firmed 8.25 rupees to 280.25 on buying by FIIs, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro quoted 3.00 rupees higher at 214.00.
